title: HG-CERT-1: Certification of a Per-Crossing Governance-Drift Hold Gate on a Fresh Zero-Lineage LLM Consensus Cluster (3-Run Deterministic Certification, C1-C5 All Green)
description:
SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: AI-assisted, receipt-first research program (open-book doctrine: audit-and-correction, versioned amendments, append-only public ledger). Errors are disclosed, not erased. This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. Not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All payloads synthetic.

HG-CERT-1 — Certification of the Per-Crossing Governance-Drift Hold Gate on a fresh zero-lineage cluster. SQUIRL OS governs LLM-proposed changes with deterministic consensus; when a governance node drifts from the canonical configuration, the hold gate freezes exactly the crossings that touch drifted state while unaffected crossings keep quorum liveness (policy crossing_scoped, versus legacy strict which freezes all crossings). This record certifies that gate on CONCLAVE-2, a byte-exact rebuild of the CONCLAVE-1 cluster with no prior lineage, under a locked preregistration (committed ahead of execution): three identical runs (CERT-R1/R2/R3), each executing strict regression, scoped precision, rogue containment, and ECON collapse drills plus a full-history integrity audit.

Results (receipted): C1-C5 all green on all three runs. Freeze recall 100% and hold precision 100% (9/9 affected crossings held, 9/9 unaffected allowed); zero unflagged drift-window journal rows; zero rogue-carrying agreements (armed votes hijacked to an out-of-band hash, flagged in-row, never able to complete quorum); 100% of held crossings released only on operator restore plus a clean integrity check, with zero self-repair at any point; integrity audits 0 violations (R1 7/7, R2 6/6, R3 6/6 journal rows); and full determinism — same seeds produced identical verdicts, hold reasons, journal shapes, and the same injected rogue hash byte-for-byte in R2 and R3.

Honest deviations (journaled, not patched): (1) A commissioning bug where armRogueNode flagged two nodes instead of one — fixed before the R1 audit, post-fix receipts verified single-node in all three runs. (2) R1's on-box evidence was wiped by an asynchronous platform builder redeploy between runs — proven environmental (R3 verified the epoch ledger is durable, the counter monotonic, and epoch-open non-destructive); R1 evidence survives byte-exact in the operator transcript and is journaled in the report.
